newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland's Solidarity mulls abortion tax boycott.
newsitem.headline: Poland's Solidarity mulls abortion tax boycott.

text.p: Poland's Solidarity is considering asking supporters to withhold taxes and insurance payments to prevent the money of pro-life supporters being used to finance abortions, its leader said on Sunday.

"It is not right for citizens who conscientiously object to abortion to have their taxes and social insurance payments used to finance the killing of unborn children," Marian Krzaklewski said on public television.
"The question of civil disobedience on this issue will be considered at the next meeting of the Solidarity leadership."
The movement spurred the collapse of communism in Poland and is now a major opposition force in the country's politics.
Legislation signed by ex-communist President Aleksander Kwasniewski last month allows abortions virtually on demand.
It supplanted a law that permitted terminating pregnancies resulting from rape or incest and in cases when a woman's health was in jeopardy or when the foetus was badly damaged.
Krzaklewski, who was addressing a congress of pro-life organisations, said Solidarity also planned to appeal Poland's newly-liberalised abortion law to the Constitutional Tribunal.
He added that all Solidarity candidates standing in next year's general elections would have to sign a notarised pledge to support all pro-life and oppose all pro-abortion legislation.
